newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wool prices mixed but generally better at NZ sale.
newsitem.headline: Wool prices mixed but generally better at NZ sale.

text.p: Wool prices were mixed but generally improved at the sale in Dunedin on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The market indicator rose four cents to NZ$4.70. The medium segment fell five to $4.96, the strong segment rose two to $4.32 and the fine segment rose 19 cents to $8.32.

Compared with the sale at Napier on Wednesday, crossbred fleece 32/33 micron was generally 2.0 percent cheaper with the remainder up to 1.0 percent dearer. Second shear was up to 1.0 percent cheaper. Bulky skirtings were generally unchanged but second shear bellies and pieces were 2.0 percent dearer.

Compared with the sale at Christchurch on October 17, Merino fleece 18 micron was generally unchanged while the remainder was 2.0 to 3.0 percent dearer. Halfbred fleece 24 micron was up to 2.0 percent dearer and the remainder was up to 1.0 percent cheaper. Main interest came from Western Europe with support from China, local mills and Japan.

The main components were 42 percent Merino fleece, 17 percent halfbred fleece and 12 percent crossbred fleece. Passings which failed to meet growers' reserves amounted to 15 percent of the 1,773 clean tonnes on offer.
The next sale will be held at Christchurch on October 31.
